correctness.rationale: Independent analytic reconstruction. Orthogonality makes the two row-sign classes equally large and x*=0. The scalar normal equation gives (g²−h²)/(g²+h²+2ρgh+η), with an almost surely positive denominator even in the two rank-one sign classes. For |ρ|<1 and below the support endpoint, the upper tail of cos φ/(1+ρ sin φ) is the angular fraction on which cos φ−tρ sin φ>t, namely arccos(t/√(1+ρ²t²))/π. Symmetry, followed by differentiation, gives the stated absolute CDF and signed density. Orthogonal sums/differences give a standard Cauchy at |ρ|=1. Counting fair signs or the two size-N/2 populations gives all the weights, including the exact without-replacement cutoff; the largest nonextreme |ρ| is at most 1−2/m for m≥2, proving the stated support and tail separation. At the extremes the ridge squared risk is Q(η)=E[U²/(U²+η/2)²]. Scaling U=√(η/2)t gives √η Q(η)→√π/2, because the remaining integral of t²/(1+t²)² is π/2. The Gaussian-exponential error in the scaled integral is O(√η) by splitting at η^(-1/2), so the unscaled error is O(1). Away from extremes ridge only decreases squared magnitude. On |R_m|≤1/2 that magnitude is bounded by 4/3, while the nonextreme complement has contribution bounded by B_m² times the exponentially small fair-sign concentration tail. In the prefix coupling R_m→0 and η_m→0 give the arcsine variable of squared mean 1/2. Adding the exact extreme mass times Q(η_m) gives the arbitrary-sequence expansion and all three regimes, with errors governed by m and η_m, not their relative speed. The supplied script was inspected, not executed; the analytic verification does not rely on its numerical tests.
residual_risks: Scalar fixed-data instance only; no claim about general regression, ordinary signed SRHT or Gaussian pooling. The numerical coefficient uses exactly the stated ηx²/2 penalty.
